summary.intent: Integrate parallel subagent work for the v5 restructuring of the wisp-plugins repo: merge the release-script fix and the new `wisp` core plugin (one work skill plus a fresh-context verifier) into an integration branch built on the deletion branch.
summary.outcome: The release-resume fix and the wisp core branch were merged into the integration branch. The Codex catalog conflict was resolved by hand, the generated marketplace files were regenerated, and the stale `muse:component` and `muse:exit-gate` references were being fixed. The merged tree's final check status and the version/changelog inspection were not yet confirmed.

repo: Generated files (Codex marketplace files, `.agents/`, `dist/codex/`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`) are regenerated via `just marketplace-sync` and `just claude-manifests-sync`; on merge conflicts, take one side and regenerate rather than hand-merge.
`harnesses/codex/catalog.json` is hand-maintained and conflicted on merge; it needed a manual resolution.
`just check` runs the whole suite (223 tests on the wisp branch). New concern directories under `shared/references/` must be added to `CONCERN_DIRECTORIES` in `tests/test_reference_integrity.py`.
`shared/hooks/validate-handback.py` routes agents to schemas. After the old plugins are deleted it should route only `wisp:verifier` (and no longer `muse:exit-gate`).
The Codex description budget is 8000 characters; wisp brings it to 7907 until the old plugins are removed.

After the delete track, `tests/test_prompt_alignment.py` (needs at least 5 exit gates) and `tests/test_agent_structure.py` (needs at least 40 agents) will fail, and `route-guard.py` and `shared/references/architecture/modes.md` still reference retired plugins.
ADR 018 supersedes ADR 003 and 007 and partially supersedes 001, but `shared/constitution.md` still describes cognitive-mode separation.
workflow: Switching branches reverts files that live only on another branch (such as the release.py fix), so the fix branch had to be merged into the integration branch explicitly.
Subagent hand-back reports are model output and need verification on the merged tree; here the integration run exposed three failures the subagent's isolated check did not.

friction: Merge conflict in `harnesses/codex/catalog.json` and the generated Codex marketplace files.
Merged tree had three failing tests from stale `muse:component` references in wisp and the handback route for the deleted `muse:exit-gate`.
Branch switching reverted release.py and its test to the deletion branch's version.
open_items: The `wisp-packs` subagent was still running and has not been merged.
Update `tests/test_prompt_alignment.py`, `tests/test_agent_structure.py`, `route-guard.py` and `architecture/modes.md` for the retired plugins.
The wisp Stop hook was never tested in a live Claude Code session, nor was the Codex bundle on Codex itself.
The adversary reuses `candidate-assessment@1`, which requires a file and line, so claims without a code location fit poorly.
Decide whether to keep the stop-check hook's per-session fingerprint rule that the subagent added beyond spec.
Version sources and changelog tops were being inspected (likely for a release bump); that work is unfinished.
Nothing has been pushed; the wisp commit and the integration branch are local only.
